newsitem.title: USA: Wal-Mart has higher third quarter.
newsitem.headline: Wal-Mart has higher third quarter.

text.p: Wal-Mart Stores Inc., the nation's largest retailer, Tuesday reported higher earnings for the third quarter on a 12 percent gain in sales.
Strength for the quarter came from the Wal-Mart stores division, including the company's Supercenters, as well as its Sam's Club warehouse stores.

For the quarter, Wal-Mart earned $684 million, or 30 cents a share, just shy of analysts' average projections of 31 cents a share, according to First Call, which tracks Wall Street earnings projections. Revenues were $25.6 billion.
A year earlier it earned $612 million, or 27 cents a share, on revenues of $22.9 billion.

The International Division had an operating loss of $15 million for the quarter, compared with a loss of $10 million last year, due to large start-up expenses, the company said. In the fiscal year to date, Wal-Mart opened 21 international units, one in Argentina, four in Canada, two in China, one in Indonesia and 13 in Mexico.
The company said its Sam's division had an operating profit for the quarter of $207 million, up 5 percent from $197 million in the year-ago period.

Looking at the fourth quarter, traditionally retailers' strongest, President and CEO David Glass said, "The company is well positioned for the holiday season and we have an excellent opportunity to reach our goals for the fourth quarter and the year."

Since the begining of its fiscal year, Wal-Mart opened 40 discount stores and relocated or expanded 13 additional stores. It opened 96 Supercenters, including 87 discount store replacements. It opened eight new Sam's Clubs, and closed four Clubs.
Wal-Mart's stock was off $1.375 at $25.125 in midday trading on the New York Stock Exchange.
